title: The Half-Light Language
premise: Silas Almeida, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost his sense of taste twelve years ago, has built his career on beautiful evasions — until Mireia, the last fluent speaker of Vessic, a dying coastal language of taste and tide, asks him to become her final student. As he learns that Vessic has no word for 'lie' but forty for kinds of silence, he discovers his late mother was the language's disgraced first student, and that his own numbness began the night she left. Returning to the fishing village where her story went wrong, Silas must choose between protecting the found family that raised him and telling the truth that could restore both the language and his tongue. In the end, he speaks the unspeakable at Mireia's deathbed, tastes salt for the first time in twelve years, and becomes not the last speaker but the first of a new line.
about_author: Ansel Eriksen is the pen name of a former line cook who spent six years in kitchens along the northern Atlantic before turning to writing. Their essays on food, memory, and silence have appeared in small literary journals, and 'The Half-Light Language' is their first novel.

chapters.title: The Critic Who Tasted Nothing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet him writing a rave review of a meal he cannot taste, performing delight from muscle memory and old notes. A young chef he once destroyed recognizes his fraud in a quiet kitchen confrontation. The emotional beat is shame disguised as professionalism; Silas realizes his whole life is the art of almost saying it.

chapters.title: A Letter in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A letter arrives from Mireia Ondiz, an elderly woman in the village of Portell, asking him to study Vessic — the language his mother spoke and abandoned. He learns she was his mother's teacher. The beat is dread mixed with longing: the past has found his return address.

chapters.title: Forty Kinds of Silence
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, arriving in Portell. Mireia begins lessons: Vessic names silences the way other languages name colors. He meets Tomas, the fisherman who raised him after his mother left, and feels the village watching. The beat is disorientation — every lesson sounds like an accusation he can't yet translate.

chapters.title: What My Mother Carried
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Mireia's journal entries. Silas finds his mother's old notebooks in Mireia's attic: she recorded Vessic faithfully until a final torn page. Mireia reveals the village blamed her for something Silas never knew. The beat is the first crack in loyalty — the found family may have lied to protect him.

chapters.title: The Word for Betrayal
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. We learn what the village believes: Silas's mother stole Mireia's recordings and sold them to a university, dooming the language's preservation. Tomas has spent thirty years keeping this from Silas out of love. The beat is protective grief — loyalty as a kind of burial.

chapters.title: Lessons in the Half-Light
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Winter deepens; lessons move to Mireia's kitchen, where she teaches through cooking, naming flavors in Vessic. For one blinding moment Silas almost tastes her fish stew — then loses it. Mireia's health fails visibly. The beat is hunger: he wants the truth as badly as he wants taste.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Mireia's POV. She finally tells Silas the truth she has carried: his mother never betrayed her — Mireia accused her falsely, in grief and jealousy, and the village made the lie permanent. His mother fled rather than fight a language community that had no word for taking it back. The beat is devastating release and new guilt.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is Also a Silence
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Confronting Tomas, Silas must decide whether exposing the old lie destroys the only family he has left. Tomas confesses he always suspected but chose Mireia over the truth. The beat is rupture: love without honesty revealed as its own half-light, dim and habitable but not whole.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, climax. On Mireia's deathbed, before the gathered village, Silas speaks in Vessic for the first time — publicly restoring his mother's name and Mireia's confession together, refusing the comfort of either silence. Some villagers turn away; others begin answering him in the old tongue. The beat is terrible, necessary exposure.

chapters.title: Salt
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, months later. Mireia is buried; a handful of villagers, including a changed Tomas, attend weekly lessons Silas now leads. Eating alone at a harbor table, he tastes salt — ordinary, imperfect, real. He writes a review that finally tells the truth about himself. The beat is quiet resurrection: inheritance accepted, family remade in honesty.
